model_note: Manager runs as `claude -p` with the CLI default model. Every worker you dispatch (editor_error, editor_success, ranker, learning_rate, slow_update, meta_memory, skill_reviewer) is `claude -p "$(cat <filled>)" --model sonnet` (single-shot, no tools). Rollouts go through harness/rollout_batch.py --backend claude and inherit SKILL_TRAINER_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 from train.sh; never override the rollout model per call.
boundary: Bounded validation run. After logging the results.tsv row for STEP 8 (and, if you reach it, the epoch-1 boundary rows), write runs/j01/TERMINAL as `exhausted: step boundary 8 reached` and stop. Never run past step 8.
gate_note: Single-mode run: this is a judge-mode suite (scoring.md default_mode=judge) where cheap == full, so cheap is the authoritative mode and the best tag moves on cheap accept_new_best. Paired gate per PROGRAM section 4f: the 3 baseline val scores.json files are the reference set, replaced by the accepted candidate's val scores.json after every accept. Primary suite name is `review` (every task carries suite=review); no secondary suite; mixed weight 0.5. Scoring: `$PY harness/score.py --suite tasks/skill-review --batch <out> --jobs 4` (rollout_batch --score does this for you). Receipts for judge-mode suites MUST include the judge's feedback: from each scored workspace's judge.json take samples[0].reasoning plus the per-criterion evidence strings, capped to the 40-line receipt limit (PROGRAM section 4a). HYPOTHESIS under test: the structured LLM-judge feedback is enough signal for editors to rebuild the review checklist that the weakened skill lacks (defect classes: invalid/reserved names, description voice/trigger/length, Windows paths, nested references, time-sensitive text, option lists without defaults, inconsistent terms, obvious explanations, extraneous files, missing scripts, magic numbers, second-person body, buried quick start, directory/name mismatch, undocumented binaries). Success = val mixed rising above the baseline through accepted steps.
